title: Security-vs-Innovation National Framing x Eval Non-Harmonization: Simulating Coordination Breakdown

original_idea.body:
# Security-vs-Innovation National Framing x Eval Non-Harmonization: Simulating Coordination Breakdown

**Problem:** Failure mode A: national institutes adopt divergent framings (UK 'AI Security Institute' vs US 'CAISI' innovation framing), implying different eval priorities. Failure mode B: there is no harmonized eval methodology. Together, the same model can pass one nation's bar and fail another's, enabling jurisdiction-shopping — a compound failure of international coordination.

**Direction:** Construct a small toy 'two-regulator' model: define two stylized eval batteries (security-weighted vs innovation/utility-weighted) over a handful of measurable axes, score several open models on each, and show how often the pass/fail verdicts disagree. Map disagreement onto a simple jurisdiction-shopping incentive. Mostly analysis with a light empirical scoring component.

**Why it matters:** Turns the surprising UK/US renaming divergence into a measurable coordination-risk metric for the International Network of AI Safety Institutes. Cheap, public-model, and squarely outside any single lab's interest.

**Relevant context:** UK AISI -> AI Security Institute, US AISI -> CAISI divergence (subfield context); International consensus on eval methodologies open problem (FLI; interface-eu.org).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain on jurisdiction-shopping but the two stylized eval batteries are speculative, weakening the link.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Toy two-regulator scoring on open models; accessible, single GPU/API.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused disagreement-measurement study, some design judgment on the stylized batteries.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public models; independent coordination-risk modeling labs won't do.

low_compute.reasoning: Light inference on open models, single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: The jurisdiction-shopping framing applied to a toy model appears partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The toy two-regulator jurisdiction-shopping model appears partly open.
